programme: A brain-microenvironment stress-adaptation and dedifferentiation module built on ATF5 (integrated-stress-response bZIP factor that blocks terminal glial/neuronal differentiation and sustains progenitor-like survival), JUNB (AP-1 subunit that reprograms tumor-associated microglia/myeloid cells and modulates immune checkpoint signaling), and SOX4 (SOX-family factor sustaining a neural-crest/neuroepithelial stem-like, migratory state via targets such as SOX2, CDH2, NCAM1 and EGFR).
role_in_a: In melanoma, ATF5 is a validated survival/therapeutic node — cell-penetrating peptides co-targeting ATF5 with CEBPB/CEBPD sensitize melanoma cells to NK-cell killing (42121927, 40358191); JUNB marks microglia within the melanoma brain-metastasis microenvironment and intersects with S1P/S1P1 signaling in brain-tropic melanoma cells (37894348, 41097703); SOX4 drives drug resistance and is implicated specifically in melanoma brain metastasis programmes (40396326, 36435874).
role_in_b: In lower-grade glioma/glioblastoma, ATF5 is a well-characterized driver that blocks astrocyte/progenitor differentiation and sustains glioma cell survival, validated across models and reviewed as a cross-cancer target (28480569, 28718401); JUNB participates in glioma immune evasion through the ATXN3–PD-L1 axis and in radiosensitivity stratification via S100A9/RAGE (38038129, 35411077); SOX4 has a documented dual oncogenic/tumor-suppressive role in glioblastoma and promotes a stem-like migratory phenotype in glioma (41776093, 23204229).
shared_axis: Melanoma cells that colonize the brain and glioma cells that are native to it face the same CNS niche, and both appear to lean on the same stress-survival/dedifferentiation transcriptional toolkit — ATF5 blocking terminal differentiation, JUNB reshaping the local myeloid/microglial and immune-checkpoint environment, and SOX4 preserving a neural stem-like, invasive state — so the recurrence looks like convergent adaptation to a shared tissue niche rather than a shared cell of origin.
reasoning: Each factor is independently and specifically documented in both diseases, including papers that explicitly study both together (37894348, 38038129, 35411077 on JUNB; 23204229, 36435874, 35538578, 37958409 on SOX4), so the module is nameable and partly placed by the retrieved record rather than pure inference. It falls short of 'established' because no source states melanoma and glioma share this axis as a field-level fact, and the three carrying factors have only mid-range recurrence (93–104 of 207 comparisons) — notably lower than the top-recurring factor CEBPA (120/207), which lacks any glioma-side evidence and so cannot anchor the cross-disease claim.
support: 42121927 — Dpep peptide co-targeting ATF5/CEBPB/CEBPD synergizes with NK cell killing in melanoma; 40358191 — companion study, same ATF5/CEBPB/CEBPD peptide sensitizes tumor cells to NK-92MI cytotoxicity; 28480569 — ATF5 expression and targeting demonstrated in canine (comparative) gliomas; 28718401 — review of ATF5 as a therapeutic target across cancers including glioma and melanoma; 37894348 — JunB-expressing microglia identified as a driver within the melanoma brain-metastasis microenvironment; 38038129 — CRISPR screen links glioma ATXN3 deubiquitylase to PD-L1-positive immune regulation; 35411077 — S100A9/RAGE axis stratifies radiosensitivity of brain metastases; 41097703 — S1P/S1P1 signaling links brain-metastasizing melanoma to the brain microenvironment; 40396326 — SOX4 inhibition resensitizes drug-resistant melanoma to cisplatin; 41776093 — SOX4 shown to have a dual regulatory role in glioblastoma; 23204229 — loss of miR-204 enhances glioma migration and stem-cell-like phenotype via a SOX4-linked axis; 36435874 — molecular programmes decoded in melanoma brain metastases including SOX4; 37958409 — pan-cancer validation of SOX4 as a diagnostic/prognostic/immune marker spanning both tumor types.
how_to_falsify: Knock down ATF5, JUNB, and SOX4 individually and in combination in a brain-tropic melanoma line and a patient-derived LGG/GBM line cultured under matched CNS-mimetic (hypoxic, astrocyte-conditioned) conditions: the shared-programme account predicts coordinated loss of stemness/differentiation-block markers (e.g. SOX2, CDH2, NCAM1) and reduced viability in both lineages, plus reduced JUNB+ myeloid/microglial recruitment in co-culture or matched melanoma-brain-metastasis versus primary glioma tissue sections. If only one lineage responds, or the three factors do not co-vary, the shared axis is falsified.
caveats: Tissue pairing is brain|skin with 207 patient-group comparisons but only 1 independent cohort pair, so replication across separate patient cohorts has not been tested. The single-view exclusions (E2F4, GCM1, ARID5A, etc.) confirm the three carrying factors are not one-subgroup artifacts. The tissue-generic exclusion list (RFX5, HDAC7, STAT4, FOXP3, EGR4) removed the obvious generic immune regulators, so the JUNB-based immune/microglial claim rests only on the specific JUNB evidence retrieved, not on a broader documented immune axis — it should not be over-read as a general immune-infiltration story. CEBPA, the single highest-recurrence factor (120/207), is deliberately excluded from the carrying set because the record shows no glioma-side evidence for it.
